ai.description: This toad reaches 8–10 cm. It is brown with dark dorsal markings and a pale belly. Distinctive features include a fleshy snout projection and prominent, triangular skin folds above each eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys robusta* is best distinguished by its exceptionally large, prominent, and triangular dermal horn-like projections on the upper eyelids compared to other species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys robusta* inhabits moist, evergreen broadleaf forests in the Eastern Himalayas, typically found at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Bengal Spadefoot Toad is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter during the day to ambush passing insects with its powerful, sticky tongue.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys robusta* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August), depositing small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys robusta* is found in the Eastern Himalayas, specifically within the Indian states of West Bengal and Arunachal Pradesh, at elevations between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Bengal Spadefoot Toad produces a single, low-pitched "cluck" or "bonk" sound, typically heard echoing from rocky stream beds in dense, humid forests.
